subject: Physics
examFormat: Three papers (1, 2 and 3), all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 are a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: fifty multiple-choice questions, 1 1/4 hours, 50 marks. Paper 2: Section A has seven short-structured questions (answer any five, 15 marks) and Section B has five essay questions (answer any three, 45 marks), 1 1/2 hours, 60 marks. Paper 3: practical test (alternative to practical paper for private candidates) with three questions, answer any two, 2 3/4 hours, 50 marks. Questions are set in S.I. units.
excluded: Preamble, aims, assessment objectives and scheme of examination (summarised in examFormat). The syllabus has no country split; the Harmonised Topics for short structured questions are included as the final topics. A page of the source that repeated items 25(f)-(h), 26 and 27(a) was de-duplicated.

topics.name: Concepts of matter
objectives: Discuss the simple structure of matter
Treat the three physical states of matter: solid, liquid and gas
Give evidence of the particle nature of matter, e.g. Brownian motion experiment and the kinetic theory of matter
Use the kinetic theory to explain states of matter, pressure in a gas, evaporation and boiling, cohesion, adhesion and capillarity
Compare crystalline and amorphous substances and describe the arrangement of atoms in a crystalline structure, e.g. face centred, body centred

topics.name: Fundamental and derived quantities and units
topics.content: Fundamental quantities: length, mass, time, electric current, luminous intensity, thermodynamic temperature and amount of substance, with m, kg, s, A, cd, K and mol as their respective units. Derived quantities: volume, density and speed, with m3, kg m-3 and m s-1 as their respective units.

subtopics.name: Fundamental quantities and units
objectives: State the fundamental quantities and their units
Use m, kg, s, A, cd, K and mol as the units of length, mass, time, electric current, luminous intensity, thermodynamic temperature and amount of substance

subtopics.name: Derived quantities and units
objectives: State volume, density and speed as derived quantities
Use m3, kg m-3 and m s-1 as their respective units

topics.name: Position, distance and displacement
topics.content: Questions are set in S.I. units; multiples or sub-multiples may be used. Position of objects in space using the X, Y, Z axes should be mentioned. Graphical location and directions by axes are to be stressed.

subtopics.name: Concept of position
objectives: Explain position as a location of a point using rectangular coordinates
Mention the position of objects in space using the X, Y, Z axes

subtopics.name: Measurement of distance
objectives: Measure distance using string, metre rule, vernier calipers and micrometer screw gauge
Note the degree of accuracy of each instrument
State the metre (m) as the unit of distance

subtopics.name: Concept of direction
objectives: Explain direction as a way of locating a point, i.e. bearing
Use a compass and a protractor

subtopics.name: Distinction between distance and displacement
objectives: Distinguish between distance and displacement

topics.name: Mass and weight
objectives: Distinguish between mass and weight
Use the lever balance and chemical/beam balance to measure mass and the spring balance to measure weight
Mention the electronic/digital balance
State the kilogram (kg) as the unit of mass and the newton (N) as the unit of weight

topics.name: Time
objectives: Explain time as the interval between physical events
Measure time using the heart-beat, sand-clock, ticker-timer, pendulum and stopwatch/clock
State the second (s) as the unit of time

subtopics.name: Volume, density and relative density
objectives: Determine volume, density and relative density experimentally for solids and liquids

subtopics.name: Pressure in fluids
objectives: Define pressure
State and apply Pascal's principle to the hydraulic press and car brakes
Explain the dependence of pressure on the depth of a point below a liquid surface
Describe atmospheric pressure
Describe the simple barometer, manometer, siphon, syringe and pump
Determine the relative density of liquids with the U-tube and Hare's apparatus

subtopics.name: Equilibrium of bodies
objectives: Identify the forces acting on a body partially or completely immersed in a fluid

subtopics.name: Archimedes' principle
objectives: Use Archimedes' principle to determine the relative densities of solids and liquids

subtopics.name: Law of flotation
objectives: Establish the conditions for a body to float in a fluid
Apply the law of flotation in the hydrometer, balloons, boats, ships, submarines etc.

topics.name: Motion
topics.content: Only qualitative treatment is required for types of motion; illustrations should be given for the various types. Numerical problems on co-linear motion may be set. Experiments with a string tied to a stone at one end and whirled around should be carried out to demonstrate motion in a vertical/horizontal circle and to show the difference between angular speed and velocity; a diagram should be drawn to illustrate centripetal force, and banking of roads in reducing sideways friction should be discussed qualitatively.

subtopics.name: Types of motion
objectives: Illustrate random, rectilinear, translational, rotational, circular, orbital, spin and oscillatory motion

subtopics.name: Relative motion
objectives: Solve numerical problems on co-linear motion

subtopics.name: Cause of motion
objectives: State force as the cause of motion

subtopics.name: Types of force
objectives: Distinguish contact forces (push and pull) from non-contact (field) forces
Give examples of field forces: electric and magnetic attractions and repulsions, gravitational pull

subtopics.name: Solid friction
objectives: Distinguish frictional force between two stationary bodies (static) from that between two bodies in relative motion (dynamic)
Define coefficients of limiting friction and determine them
State the advantages of friction, e.g. in locomotion, friction belt, grindstone
State the disadvantages of friction, e.g. reduction of efficiency, wear and tear of machines
Describe methods of reducing friction, e.g. ball bearings, rollers, streamlining and lubrication

subtopics.name: Viscosity (friction in fluids)
objectives: Define viscosity and state its effects
Explain viscosity as an extension of friction in fluids
Treat fluid friction and its application in lubrication qualitatively
Explain terminal velocity and its determination

subtopics.name: Simple ideas of circular motion
objectives: Demonstrate motion in a vertical/horizontal circle
Show the difference between angular speed and velocity
Draw a diagram to illustrate centripetal force
Discuss banking of roads in reducing sideways friction qualitatively

subtopics.name: Concept of speed
objectives: Define speed as change of distance with time
State the metre per second (m s-1) as the unit of speed/velocity

subtopics.name: Concept of velocity
objectives: Define velocity as change of displacement with time
Use a ticker-timer or similar device to determine speed/velocity

subtopics.name: Uniform and non-uniform speed/velocity
objectives: Distinguish between uniform and non-uniform speed/velocity

subtopics.name: Distance/displacement-time graph
objectives: Determine instantaneous speed/velocity from a distance/displacement-time graph and by calculation

subtopics.name: Concept of acceleration and deceleration
objectives: Define acceleration/deceleration as increase/decrease in velocity with time
State the unit of acceleration as m s-2
Use a ticker timer or similar device to determine acceleration

subtopics.name: Uniform and non-uniform acceleration
objectives: Distinguish between uniform and non-uniform acceleration

subtopics.name: Velocity-time graph
objectives: Determine acceleration and displacement from a velocity-time graph

subtopics.name: Equations of motion with constant acceleration
objectives: Use the equations of motion to solve numerical problems
Treat motion under gravity as a special case

topics.name: Scalars and vectors
topics.content: Mass, distance, speed and time are examples of scalars; weight, displacement, velocity and acceleration are examples of vectors. A force board is used to determine the resultant of two forces.

subtopics.name: Concept of scalars
objectives: Define scalars as physical quantities with magnitude and no direction

subtopics.name: Concept of vectors
objectives: Define vectors as physical quantities with both magnitude and direction

subtopics.name: Vector representation
objectives: Represent vectors

subtopics.name: Addition of vectors
objectives: Add vectors, using a force board to determine the resultant of two forces

subtopics.name: Resolution of vectors
objectives: Resolve vectors

subtopics.name: Resultant velocity using vector representation
objectives: Obtain the resultant of two velocities analytically and graphically

subtopics.name: Principle of moments
objectives: State and apply the principle of moments
Explain torque/moment of force
Give a simple treatment of a couple, e.g. turning of a water tap, corkscrew and steering wheel

subtopics.name: Conditions for equilibrium of rigid bodies
objectives: State the conditions for equilibrium of rigid bodies under parallel and non-parallel forces
Use a force board to determine resultant and equilibrant forces
Resolve forces into two perpendicular directions and compose forces
Apply the parallelogram of forces and the triangle of forces

subtopics.name: Centre of gravity and stability
objectives: Treat centre of gravity and stability experimentally
Distinguish stable, unstable and neutral equilibria

topics.name: Simple harmonic motion
topics.content: Mathematical proof of simple harmonic motion for the spiral spring, bifilar suspension and loaded test-tube is not required; derivation of the formula for g is not required. Simple problems may be set.

subtopics.name: Illustration, explanation and definition of simple harmonic motion
objectives: Illustrate, explain and define simple harmonic motion (S.H.M.)
Use a loaded test-tube oscillating vertically in a liquid, simple pendulum, spiral spring and bifilar suspension to demonstrate S.H.M.

subtopics.name: Speed and acceleration of S.H.M.
objectives: Relate linear and angular speeds, and linear and angular accelerations

subtopics.name: Period, frequency and amplitude of S.H.M.
objectives: Determine 'g' experimentally with the simple pendulum and helical spring
Treat the theory of the principles of these experiments

subtopics.name: Energy of S.H.M.
objectives: Solve simple problems on simple harmonic motion

subtopics.name: Forced vibration and resonance
objectives: Explain forced vibration and resonance

topics.name: Newton's laws of motion
topics.content: The relationship between acceleration and force is investigated with timing devices, e.g. a ticker-timer to determine the acceleration of a falling body when the accelerating force is constant.

subtopics.name: First Law: inertia of rest and inertia of motion
objectives: State the first law
Explain inertia of rest and inertia of motion
Distinguish between inertia mass and weight

subtopics.name: Second Law: force, acceleration, momentum and impulse
objectives: State the second law
Define force, momentum and impulse
Use timing devices to determine the acceleration of a falling body
Explain linear momentum and its conservation
Treat collision of elastic bodies in a straight line

subtopics.name: Third Law: action and reaction
objectives: State the third law
Apply it to the recoil of a gun, jet and rocket propulsions

topics.name: Energy
topics.content: Forms of energy: mechanical (potential and kinetic), heat, chemical, electrical, light, sound, nuclear. Renewable (e.g. solar, wind, tides, hydro, ocean waves) and non-renewable (e.g. petroleum, coal, nuclear, biomass) sources of energy should be discussed briefly.

subtopics.name: Forms of energy
objectives: Give examples of the various forms of energy

subtopics.name: World energy resources
objectives: Discuss briefly renewable and non-renewable sources of energy

subtopics.name: Conservation of energy
objectives: State the principle of conservation of energy
Use it to explain energy transformations

topics.name: Work, energy and power
topics.content: The joule (J) is the unit of energy; the unit of electrical consumption is kWh. The derivations of P.E. and K.E. are expected to be known.

subtopics.name: Concept of work
objectives: Explain work as a measure of energy transfer
State the joule (J) as the unit of energy

subtopics.name: Concept of energy
objectives: Explain energy as the capability to do work

subtopics.name: Work done in a gravitational field
objectives: Calculate work done in lifting a body and by falling bodies

subtopics.name: Types of mechanical energy
objectives: Derive and use potential energy (P.E.) and kinetic energy (K.E.)
Identify the types of energy possessed by a body under given conditions

subtopics.name: Conservation of mechanical energy
objectives: Verify the principle of conservation of mechanical energy

subtopics.name: Concept of power
objectives: Define power as the time rate of doing work
State the watt (W) as the unit of power

subtopics.name: Application of mechanical energy: machines
objectives: Treat levers, pulleys, inclined plane, wedge, screw, wheel and axle, and gears
Treat the force ratio (F.R.), mechanical advantage (M.A.), velocity ratio (V.R.) and efficiency of each machine
Identify the simple machines that make up a complicated machine, e.g. a bicycle
Explain the effects of friction on machines and the reduction of friction in machines

topics.name: Heat energy
topics.content: The kinetic theory is used to explain the effects of heat. Per Kelvin (K-1) is the unit of expansivity; J kg-1 K-1 is the unit of specific heat capacity; J kg-1 is the unit of specific latent heat.

subtopics.name: Temperature and its measurement
objectives: Explain temperature as the degree of hotness or coldness of a body
Describe the construction and graduation of a simple thermometer
State the properties of thermometric liquids
Treat the constant-volume gas thermometer, resistance thermometer, thermocouple, liquid-in-glass thermometer (including maximum and minimum and clinical thermometers); mention the pyrometer
Use the Celsius and Absolute scales, with kelvin and degree Celsius as units

subtopics.name: Effects of heat on matter
objectives: Explain rise in temperature, change of phase state, expansion and change of resistance using the kinetic theory
Mention change of colour, thermionic emission and change in chemical properties

subtopics.name: Thermal expansion
objectives: Treat linear, area and volume expansivities qualitatively and quantitatively
Describe consequences and applications of expansion in buildings and bridges, bimetallic strips, thermostat, overhead cables and railway lines
Explain real and apparent expansion of liquids and the anomalous expansion of water

subtopics.name: Heat transfer
objectives: Describe conduction, convection and radiation using the kinetic theory
Give simple experimental illustrations
Explain land and sea breezes, ventilation and applications in cooling devices
Describe the vacuum flask

subtopics.name: The gas laws
objectives: Verify Boyle's law, Charles' law, the pressure law and the general gas law using simple apparatus
Use the kinetic theory to explain the laws and solve simple problems
Mention the operation of safety air bags in vehicles

subtopics.name: Measurement of heat energy
objectives: Explain heat capacity and specific heat capacity
Determine specific heat capacities of solids and liquids by the method of mixtures and the electrical method
Relate land and sea breezes to the specific heat capacity of water and land

subtopics.name: Latent heat
objectives: Explain the concept and types of latent heat
Determine the melting point of a solid and the boiling point of a liquid
Explain the effects of impurities and pressure on melting and boiling points, with application in the pressure cooker
Determine specific latent heats of fusion of ice and of vaporization of steam by the method of mixtures and the electrical method
Describe applications in refrigerators and air conditioners

subtopics.name: Evaporation and boiling
objectives: Discuss the effect of temperature, humidity, surface area and draught on evaporation

subtopics.name: Vapour and vapour pressure
objectives: Explain vapour and vapour pressure
Demonstrate vapour pressure with simple experiments
Explain saturated vapour pressure and its relation to boiling

subtopics.name: Humidity, relative humidity and dew point
objectives: Measure dew point and relative humidity
Estimate the humidity of the atmosphere using a wet and dry-bulb hygrometer

subtopics.name: Humidity and the weather
objectives: Explain the formation of dew, fog and rain

topics.name: Production and propagation of waves
topics.content: Ropes and springs (slinky) are used to generate mechanical waves; the ripple tank shows water waves and demonstrates energy propagation by waves. The hertz (Hz) is the unit of frequency. Simple problems on v = f x wavelength and T = 1/f may be set.

subtopics.name: Production and propagation of mechanical waves
objectives: Describe the production and propagation of mechanical waves

subtopics.name: Pulsating system
objectives: Explain that energy is transmitted with definite speed, frequency and wavelength

subtopics.name: Waveform
objectives: Describe and represent a waveform graphically
Define amplitude, wavelength, frequency and period
Describe sound and light as wave phenomena

subtopics.name: Mathematical relationship connecting f, wavelength, T and v
objectives: Use the relationship between frequency, wavelength, period and velocity to solve simple problems

topics.name: Types of waves
topics.content: Questions on phase difference will not be set.

subtopics.name: Transverse and longitudinal waves
objectives: Distinguish transverse from longitudinal waves with examples

subtopics.name: Mathematical representation of wave motion
objectives: Explain the equation y = A sin(wt +/- phase)

topics.name: Properties of waves
objectives: Describe reflection, refraction, diffraction, interference, and superposition of progressive waves producing standing (stationary) waves
Demonstrate these properties with plane and circular waves using the ripple tank
Explain the properties

subtopics.name: Sources of light
objectives: Distinguish natural and artificial sources
Distinguish luminous and non-luminous bodies

subtopics.name: Rectilinear propagation of light
objectives: Explain the formation of shadows and eclipse
Describe the pinhole camera
Solve simple numerical problems

subtopics.name: Reflection of light at plane surfaces
objectives: Distinguish regular and irregular reflections
Verify the laws of reflection
Describe formation of images, inclined plane mirrors and rotation of mirrors
Describe applications in periscope, sextant and kaleidoscope

subtopics.name: Reflection of light at curved surfaces
objectives: State the laws of reflection and describe the formation and characteristics of images in concave and convex mirrors
Use the mirror formulae (1/u + 1/v = 1/f and magnification) to solve numerical problems (derivation not required)
Determine the focal length of a concave mirror experimentally
Describe applications in searchlight, parabolic and driving mirrors, car headlamps etc.

subtopics.name: Refraction of light at plane surfaces
objectives: State the laws of refraction
Describe formation of images, real and apparent depths
Explain critical angle and total internal reflection
Explain lateral displacement and angle of deviation in rectangular and triangular prisms
Use the minimum deviation equation n = sin((A + Dm)/2) / sin(A/2) (derivation not required)
Describe applications: periscope, prism binoculars, optical fibres and the mirage

subtopics.name: Refraction of light at curved surfaces
objectives: Describe the formation of images by converging and diverging lenses
Use the lens formulae (1/u + 1/v = 1/f and magnification) to solve numerical problems (derivation not required)
Determine the focal length of a converging lens experimentally
State the power of a lens in dioptres (D)

subtopics.name: Application of lenses in optical instruments
objectives: Describe the simple camera, the human eye, film projector, simple and compound microscopes, and terrestrial and astronomical telescopes
Explain angular magnification and describe prism binoculars
Compare the structure and function of the camera and the human eye
Describe defects of the human eye and their corrections

subtopics.name: Dispersion of white light by a triangular glass prism
objectives: Produce a pure spectrum of white light and recombine its components
Explain the colours of objects
Describe the mixing of coloured lights

topics.name: Electromagnetic waves
objectives: Describe elementary the types of radiation in the electromagnetic spectrum: radio, infrared, visible light, ultra-violet, X-rays and gamma rays
State the uses of the various types of radiation

subtopics.name: Sources of sound
objectives: Identify sources of sound

subtopics.name: Transmission of sound waves
objectives: Perform an experiment to show that a material medium is required for sound

subtopics.name: Speed of sound in solid, liquid and air
objectives: Compare the speed of sound in solid, liquid and air
Consider the dependence of the velocity of sound on temperature and pressure

subtopics.name: Echoes and reverberation
objectives: Describe the use of echoes in mineral exploration and determination of ocean depth
Give thunder and multiple reflections in a large room as examples of reverberation

subtopics.name: Noise and music
objectives: Distinguish between noise and music

subtopics.name: Characteristics of sound
objectives: Explain pitch, loudness and quality

subtopics.name: Vibration in strings
objectives: Use the sonometer to demonstrate the dependence of frequency on length, tension and mass per unit length of a string
Use the formula f = (1/2l) sqrt(T/m) in simple numerical problems
Describe applications in stringed instruments, e.g. guitar, piano, harp and violin

subtopics.name: Forced vibration
objectives: Use resonance boxes and the sonometer to illustrate forced vibration

subtopics.name: Resonance, harmonics and overtones
objectives: Explain resonance
Use overtones to explain the quality of a musical note
Describe applications in percussion instruments, e.g. drum, bell, cymbals, xylophone

subtopics.name: Vibration of air in pipes: open and closed pipes
objectives: Measure the velocity of sound in air or the frequency of a tuning fork using the resonance tube
Use the relationship v = f x wavelength in numerical problems
Mention end correction
Describe applications in wind instruments, e.g. organ, flute, trumpet, horn, clarinet and saxophone

topics.name: Description and properties of fields
topics.content: A compass needle and iron filings are used to show magnetic field lines.

subtopics.name: Concept of fields
objectives: Explain the concept of gravitational, electric and magnetic fields

subtopics.name: Properties of a force field
objectives: State the properties of a force field

topics.name: Gravitational field
topics.content: Masses include protons, electrons and planets.

subtopics.name: Acceleration due to gravity
objectives: Mention G as gravitational field intensity, g = F/m

subtopics.name: Gravitational force between two masses: Newton's law of gravitation
objectives: State Newton's law of gravitation
Use the universal gravitational constant (G)
Relate 'G' and 'g'

subtopics.name: Gravitational potential and escape velocity
objectives: Calculate the escape velocity of a rocket from the earth's gravitational field

topics.name: Electric field
topics.content: The derivation of formulae for capacitance is not required.

subtopics.name: Production of electric charges
objectives: Describe the production of charges by friction, induction and contact
Use a simple electroscope to detect and compare charges on differently-shaped bodies

subtopics.name: Types of distribution of charges
objectives: Describe distribution of charges and its application in light conductors

subtopics.name: Storage of charges
objectives: Describe the storage of charges

subtopics.name: Electric lines of force
objectives: Determine properties and field patterns of charges

subtopics.name: Electric force between point charges: Coulomb's law
objectives: State Coulomb's law
Explain the permittivity of a medium

subtopics.name: Concepts of electric field, electric field intensity and electric potential
objectives: Calculate electric field intensity and electric potential of simple systems

subtopics.name: Capacitance
objectives: Define capacitance and describe the arrangement and application of capacitors
State the factors affecting the capacitance of a parallel-plate capacitor
State the farad (F) as the unit of capacitance
Treat capacitors in series and in parallel
Explain energy stored in a charged capacitor
Describe uses of capacitors, e.g. in radio and television

subtopics.name: Production of electric current from primary and secondary cells
objectives: Describe the simple cell and its defects
Describe the Daniel cell and the Leclanche cell (wet and dry)
Describe the lead-acid accumulator and the alkaline-cadmium cell
Define the e.m.f. of a cell, with the volt (V) as its unit

subtopics.name: Potential difference and electric current
objectives: State and verify Ohm's law and define resistance
State the volt (V), ampere (A) and ohm as units of p.d., current and resistance

subtopics.name: Electric circuit
objectives: Treat series and parallel arrangement of cells and resistors
Explain lost volt and internal resistance of batteries

subtopics.name: Electric conduction through materials
objectives: Distinguish ohmic and non-ohmic conductors (metals are ohmic; semiconductors are non-ohmic)

subtopics.name: Electric energy and power
objectives: Define electrical energy and power quantitatively
Explain the heating effect of an electric current and its application
Describe conversion of electrical energy to mechanical energy, e.g. electric motors
Describe conversion of solar energy to electrical and heat energies, e.g. solar cells, solar heaters

subtopics.name: Shunt and multiplier
objectives: Describe the conversion of a galvanometer into an ammeter and a voltmeter

subtopics.name: Resistivity and conductivity
objectives: Treat the factors affecting the electrical resistance of a material
Solve simple problems

subtopics.name: Measurement of electric current, p.d., resistance, e.m.f. and internal resistance of a cell
objectives: Describe the principle of operation and use of the ammeter, voltmeter and potentiometer
Describe the Wheatstone bridge and metre bridge

topics.name: Magnetic field
topics.content: Units of magnetic flux and magnetic flux density are the weber (Wb) and the tesla (T) respectively.

subtopics.name: Properties of magnets and magnetic materials
objectives: Give practical examples such as soft iron, steel and alloys

subtopics.name: Magnetization and demagnetization
objectives: Distinguish temporary and permanent magnets
Compare iron and steel as magnetic materials

subtopics.name: Concept of magnetic field
objectives: Explain magnetic flux and magnetic flux density
Describe the magnetic field around a permanent magnet, a current-carrying conductor and a solenoid
Plot lines of force to locate neutral points

subtopics.name: Magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor and between parallel conductors
objectives: Treat the magnetic force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field and between two parallel current-carrying conductors qualitatively
Describe applications: electric motor and moving-coil galvanometer

subtopics.name: Use of electromagnets
objectives: Give examples in the electric bell, telephone earpiece etc.

subtopics.name: The earth's magnetic field
objectives: Describe the mariner's compass
Explain angles of dip and declination

subtopics.name: Magnetic force on a moving charged particle
objectives: Solve simple problems on the motion of a charged particle in a magnetic field, using F = qvB sin(theta)

topics.name: Electromagnetic field
topics.content: Direction of current, magnetic field and force in an electromagnetic field are identified using Fleming's left-hand rule. The derivation of formulae for inductance is not required.

subtopics.name: Concept of electromagnetic field
objectives: Identify the directions of current, magnetic field and force using Fleming's left-hand rule

subtopics.name: Electromagnetic induction
objectives: State Faraday's law, Lenz's law and the motor-generator effect
Describe applications: generator (d.c. and a.c.), induction coil and transformer
Treat the principles underlying the production of direct and alternating currents
Explain the equation E = Eo sin wt

subtopics.name: Inductance
objectives: Explain self and mutual inductance qualitatively
State the henry (H) as the unit of inductance
Use E = 1/2 LI squared
Describe applications in radio, T.V. and transformer

subtopics.name: Eddy currents
objectives: Treat a method of reducing eddy current losses
Describe applications in the induction furnace, speedometer etc.

subtopics.name: Power transmission and distribution
objectives: Explain the reduction of power losses in high-tension transmission lines
Discuss the household wiring system

topics.name: Simple a.c. circuits
topics.content: Derivation of formulae is not required; simple calculations and numerical problems may be set.

subtopics.name: Graphical representation of e.m.f. and current in an a.c. circuit
objectives: Treat the graphs of I = Io sin wt and E = Eo sin wt

subtopics.name: Peak and r.m.s. values
objectives: Distinguish peak and r.m.s. values
Describe the phase relationship between voltage and current in a resistor, inductor and capacitor

subtopics.name: Series circuit containing resistor, inductor and capacitor
objectives: Do simple calculations involving a.c. circuits

subtopics.name: Reactance and impedance
objectives: Treat XL and XC and impedance, solving simple numerical problems

subtopics.name: Vector diagrams
objectives: Draw vector diagrams for a.c. circuits

subtopics.name: Resonance in an a.c. circuit
objectives: Discuss applications in tuning of radio and T.V.

subtopics.name: Power in an a.c. circuit
objectives: Explain power in an a.c. circuit

subtopics.name: Models of the atom
objectives: Discuss qualitatively the Thomson, Rutherford, Bohr and electron-cloud (wave-mechanical) models
State the limitations of each model
Explain quantization of angular momentum (Bohr)

subtopics.name: Energy quantization
objectives: Explain energy levels in the atom, and colour and light frequency
Treat the Franck-Hertz experiment, line spectra from hot bodies, absorption spectra and spectra of discharge lamps

subtopics.name: Photoelectric effect
objectives: Explain the photoelectric effect and the dual nature of light
Define work function and threshold frequency
State and explain Einstein's photoelectric equation
Describe applications in T.V., camera etc. and solve simple problems

subtopics.name: Thermionic emission
objectives: Explain thermionic emission and its applications

subtopics.name: X-rays
objectives: Describe the production of X-rays and the structure of the X-ray tube
State the types, characteristics, properties, uses and hazards of X-rays and safety precautions

subtopics.name: Composition of the nucleus
objectives: Describe the nucleus as composed of protons and neutrons
Use nucleon number (A), proton number (Z), neutron number (N) and the equation A = Z + N
Describe nuclides, their notation, and isotopes

subtopics.name: Radioactivity: natural and artificial
objectives: Describe radioactive elements and radioactive emissions (alpha, beta, gamma), their properties and uses
Mention detection of radiations by G-M counter, photographic plates etc.
Explain radioactive decay, half-life and decay constant
Describe transformation of elements
Describe applications of radioactivity in agriculture, medicine, industry, archaeology etc.

subtopics.name: Nuclear reactions: fusion and fission
objectives: Distinguish between fusion and fission
Explain binding energy, mass defect and the energy equation E = (change in m)c squared
Describe nuclear reactors and the atomic bomb
State radiation hazards and safety precautions and peaceful uses of nuclear reactions

topics.name: Wave-particle paradox
topics.content: Simple illustration of the dual nature of light.

subtopics.name: Electron diffraction
objectives: Illustrate electron diffraction

subtopics.name: Duality of matter
objectives: Illustrate the duality of matter

topics.name: Derived quantities and dimensional analysis
objectives: State fundamental quantities and units, e.g. length, mass, time, electric current, luminous intensity, with m, kg, s, A, cd as their units
State derived quantities and units, e.g. volume, density, speed with m3, kg m-3, m s-1
Explain dimensions in terms of fundamental and derived quantities
Use dimensions to verify the dimensional correctness of a given equation
Use dimensions to derive the relationship between quantities
Use dimensions to obtain derived units

topics.name: Projectile motion
objectives: Explain projectiles as objects thrown or released into space
